summary: Production database security review: list every public table and function, then one reviewer per group checks RLS, policies, grants and the code paths that use them (read-only); findings with migration text and undo

findings.object: public schema default privileges (owner postgres): tables, sequences, functions
findings.what: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for role postgres in schema public still grants ALL on new tables, USAGE/SELECT/UPDATE on new sequences and EXECUTE on new functions to anon and authenticated (pg_default_acl rows postgres/r, postgres/S, postgres/f). Migration 20261016170000_browser_roles_least_privilege revoked the existing grants only, so every new users-group object goes back to browser-reachable unless that migration remembers its own REVOKE. The 17 Oct mob migration had to add its own revoke/grant block. Nothing is exposed today: all 5 tables give grants to service_role only, and 0 of the 67 public functions can be executed by anon or authenticated.
findings.scenario: A later migration adds a function such as get_my_prefs() as SECURITY DEFINER over notification_prefs or users and forgets REVOKE EXECUTE. Through the PUBLIC default, anon can call it at once via /rest/v1/rpc with the public anon key, and RLS does not protect it because a definer function bypasses RLS. A new table created with RLS forgotten is likewise fully readable and writable by anon.

findings.object: sequences public.account_deletion_requests_id_seq, public.push_devices_id_seq
findings.what: Both sequences still give USAGE, SELECT and UPDATE to anon and authenticated. The least-privilege migration loop covered relkind 'r'/'p' only and skipped sequences. This is not reachable through PostgREST today, because nextval and setval live in pg_catalog and are not exposed, and no public function exposes them. It is still leftover privilege and goes against the server-only intent.
findings.scenario: Any future exposure, such as a function granted to authenticated that calls setval, or a direct database login as authenticated, would let a browser role reset account_deletion_requests_id_seq. Inserts from requestDeletion() would then hit primary-key collisions, so deletion requests fail with DELETION_UNAVAILABLE (a denial of service on a legal data-rights flow).
findings.undo: GRANT USAGE, SELECT, UPDATE ON SEQUENCE public.account_deletion_requests_id_seq, public.push_devices_id_seq TO anon, authenticated;

findings.object: public.push_devices via src/lib/server/appPrefs.js registerDevice (POST /api/me/devices)
findings.what: registerDevice upserts with onConflict 'token' and sets user_id to the caller. Any signed-in student who submits a token that is already registered moves that token's row to their own account and clears revoked_at. Nothing checks that the token belongs to a device the caller controls. revokeDevice is scoped correctly, with eq user_id.
findings.scenario: Student B learns Student A's FCM token (from a shared or rooted device, logs, or a leaked crash report) and POSTs it to /api/me/devices. The push_devices row now has user_id = B. Once pushes are sent (no sender exists in f725a422 yet), A's phone receives B's study reminders and A stops getting their own. Impact is low today because nothing sends pushes.
findings.undo: ALTER TABLE public.push_devices DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS previous_user_id; -- and revert the registerDevice code change

findings.object: Group verdict: users, account_deletion_requests, notification_prefs, push_devices, usage_consent; account_deletion_run, auth_clear_unconfirmed_password, auth_drop_password_set_before_confirmation, enforce_admin_role
findings.what: No exploitable problem found. All 5 tables: RLS on (not forced), 0 policies, and grants to service_role only. anon and authenticated have no table or column grants, so a signed-in student cannot read or change another student's rows through PostgREST, and anon reaches nothing. No view depends on these tables, and no function executable by anon or authenticated touches them. Functions: all 4 are owned by postgres with EXECUTE for postgres and service_role only. The two SECURITY DEFINER functions (auth_clear_unconfirmed_password, auth_drop_password_set_before_confirmation) pin search_path to '' and fully qualify auth.users. The two INVOKER functions pin search_path to public, pg_temp. account_deletion_run builds dynamic SQL only with %I/%L and $1, so it is not injectable; p_steps is a server constant plan. Triggers: trg_users_enforce_admin_role (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF role,email ON public.users) and mm_drop_password_set_before_confirmation (BEFORE UPDATE OF email_confirmed_at ON auth.users). Code paths in wt-audit17: every read and write goes through supabaseAdmin(), the service role. The exported 'supabase' in src/lib/supabase.js is a proxy to the admin client. Files: data/db.js, src/lib/server/appPrefs.js, src/app/api/me/consent/route.js, src/app/api/events/route.js, src/lib/server/appErrorsStore.js, src/lib/server/accountDeletion.js (account_deletion_run RPC, operator script), src/app/api/auth/email-login/route.js (auth_clear_unconfirmed_password RPC). Browser and mobile code only call supabase.auth.*. User-scoped routes take user_id from the session (/api/users/[id] checks session.user.id === id; profilePatch whitelists name and subjects only). enforce_admin_role grants admin by a hardcoded email. That is safe because public.users rows are created only for identities with email_confirmed_at (hasConfirmedEmail in src/lib/auth.ts) and users_email_key is unique. auth_drop_password_set_before_confirmation does not need SECURITY DEFINER (it only edits NEW), but it is pinned and not callable, so this is cosmetic.
findings.scenario: No attack path found. The other three findings are latent hardening.
findings.migration: none
findings.undo: none

findings.object: schema public default privileges (owner postgres; supabase_admin too). This affects every future table, function or sequence in this group
findings.what: pg_default_acl still gives anon and authenticated ALL on new tables (arwdDxtm), EXECUTE on new functions (X) and rwU on new sequences in public, for objects created by postgres and by supabase_admin. attempts, session_check_log, sample_imports, count_distinct_mock_sessions and save_sample_import are closed today only because each migration ran an explicit REVOKE, or because 20261016170000_browser_roles_least_privilege swept them once. Nothing stops this from coming back: a new table, a replacement function made with DROP + CREATE (not CREATE OR REPLACE, which keeps the ACL) or a new RPC opens to the browser roles again. RLS would then be the only barrier, and for functions there is none.
findings.scenario: Example: a later migration drops and recreates save_sample_import, perhaps as SECURITY DEFINER so it can write past RLS, and forgets the REVOKE. anon then gets EXECUTE through the default ACL. Anyone holding the public anon key from the browser bundle can POST /rest/v1/rpc/save_sample_import with any p_user_id and write or probe sample imports for any student. The same applies to a new attempts_* table created with RLS off: anon and authenticated would get full CRUD on it.

findings.object: sequence public.sample_imports_id_seq
findings.what: anon and authenticated hold USAGE, SELECT and UPDATE on the identity sequence behind sample_imports.id (relacl: anon=rwU, authenticated=rwU). This comes from the default ACL above. Migration 20261013093000 revoked the table but not the sequence, and the 16 Oct least-privilege sweep only covered tables and functions. PostgREST and pg_graphql do not expose sequences or nextval/setval, so the browser cannot reach it today. It is a latent grant that any future anon-reachable SQL path would expose.
findings.scenario: If any anon-executable SQL path ever exists, for example a future INVOKER RPC that runs dynamic SQL, anon could call setval('public.sample_imports_id_seq', 32767 or the bigint max) or rewind it. New sample imports would then fail with 'nextval: reached maximum value', or collide on the id primary key. On a collision, save_sample_import's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING swallows the error and the fallback returns an all-NULL row. /api/me/sample-import then reports 'saved' with savedAt 1970-01-01 and 0/0 for every new student, and nothing is stored.
findings.undo: GRANT USAGE, SELECT, UPDATE ON SEQUENCE public.sample_imports_id_seq TO anon, authenticated;

findings.object: function public.save_sample_import(text,text,text,text,jsonb,int,int)
findings.what: The fallback branch at the end does not fail closed. If the INSERT is dropped by ON CONFLICT for a reason other than import_key or (user_id, sample_version), such as an id primary-key collision, both re-selects find nothing and r stays NULL. The check 'r.user_id <> p_user_id' is then NULL, not true, so it does not raise, and the function returns (false, NULL, NULL, NULL). saveSampleImport in src/lib/server/sampleImport.js turns that into status 'saved' with savedAt 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and 0/0. Security posture is otherwise right: SECURITY INVOKER, search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp', EXECUTE for service_role only. p_user_id always comes from the server session (src/app/api/me/sample-import/route.js uses session.user.id and supabaseAdmin()), and a key owned by another user raises import_key_taken, so a student cannot read or overwrite another student's import.
findings.scenario: A sequence reset (by service_role during a restore, or via the latent sequence grant) makes the next nextval collide with an existing id. The student's sample answers are silently dropped, but the app tells them 'Saved to your account'. This is an integrity bug, not a data leak.
findings.undo: Re-run the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION body from supabase/migrations/20261013093000_sample_imports.sql (identical signature; it uses '<>' and has no 'sample_import_not_saved' raise), then ALTER FUNCTION public.save_sample_import(text,text,text,text,jsonb,int,int) SET search_path = public, pg_temp; and keep REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role.

findings.object: Group summary (verified clean, no action): attempts, session_check_log, sample_imports, count_distinct_mock_sessions
findings.what: Production (isrxrxzjocewrdureyhp), read-only checks. On all three tables RLS is ON (not forced; owner is postgres) with 0 policies. Table and column grants are held by service_role only; anon, authenticated and PUBLIC have none. No triggers, no views or materialized views on top of them, not in any realtime publication. Live row counts: attempts 1816 (the reltuples estimate of 1616 is stale), session_check_log 0, sample_imports 0. Neither function is SECURITY DEFINER; both are INVOKER with search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp', and EXECUTE is held by postgres and service_role only. count_distinct_mock_sessions reads question_interactions, not attempts. Every other public function that touches these tables (finish_recovery_session, finalise_expired_recovery_session, start_learning_episode, refresh_question_option_stats, mm_leaderboard) is INVOKER with a pinned search_path and is not executable by anon or authenticated. Code in wt-audit17: every path uses the service-role client. src/lib/supabase.js exports supabase as a proxy to supabaseAdmin(), and there is no browser .from() or .rpc() on these objects. The user id always comes from the server session: api/attempts/[id] (checks attempt.userId === session.user.id; mobile/attempts/[id] re-exports it), attemptSummary (cursor is validated by ISO/ID regex and ANDed with user_id), appPrefs, timedMock, badgesStore, credits, repairRecord, repairCheckStore, nta_pool, attempt_reads, and data/db.js. Mob findAttempts reads other members' attempts by design, limited to state.members with opt-in sharing and HMAC member ids. session_check_log is reached only through api/sessions/[id]/check (feature flag SESSION_CHECK_ENABLED is off), plus the submit path and accountDeletion, always filtered by user_id. Its primary key (session_id, qid) leaves out user_id, but session ids are recovery_sessions rows owned by the user, or att_practice_ HMACs over userId, so another user cannot collide with them. save_sample_import is reached only through api/me/sample-import, and count_distinct_mock_sessions only through api/questions/[id]/interact, both with session.user.id. A signed-in student cannot read or change another student's rows, and anon can reach nothing here.
findings.scenario: None. This is the baseline for the three findings above.

findings.object: public.questions, written through POST /api/questions/[id]/interact (interaction_type 'report') in wt-audit17/src/app/api/questions/[id]/interact/route.js lines 176-200 (queueReportedQuestion)
findings.what: The route uses the service-role client (`supabase` from '@/lib/supabase' is a proxy to supabaseAdmin()). After one 'report' interaction from any signed-in user, it moves the question from live to status='pending', verification_state='disputed', exploration_state='pending_review'. There is no cap per user, no rate limit (src/proxy.js skips api/ paths), no limit of one report per user per question, and no threshold of several distinct reporters. RLS does not protect anything here because the write runs as service_role. Live state checked select-only: 101 reports from 40 reporters on 99 questions, 0 duplicate (question, user) pairs, 8,549 live questions, 367 currently held as disputed.
findings.scenario: A free student account (or a script holding any valid JWT) loops POST /api/questions/<id>/interact with {interaction_type:'report'} over every question id it sees in feeds, mocks and results. Each call pulls a live question out of practice, NTA papers, inventory counts and repairs right away (VISIBLE_QUESTION_FILTER requires status=live, or verified+active). A few thousand requests empty the live bank. Moderators then have to re-check every question by hand. The attacker reads or changes no other student's rows, but integrity and availability of the shared content are lost.

findings.object: Schema public default privileges (pg_default_acl for roles postgres and supabase_admin)
findings.what: Default privileges still give anon and authenticated full table rights (arwdDxtm) on every new table in public, EXECUTE on every new function, and rwU on sequences. Every table in this group is safe today only because each migration revoked these grants afterwards (anon and authenticated hold no grants on questions, passage_groups, question_concepts, question_version_history, question_option_stats, nta_question_index, public_inventory_snapshot or trap_atlas, and only SELECT on chapters and units). The next content table or function that misses the explicit revoke is reachable through PostgREST at once, limited only by its RLS. For functions it means callable by anon with no RLS at all.
findings.scenario: A future migration adds e.g. public.question_answer_keys or a SECURITY DEFINER helper and forgets 'revoke all ... from anon, authenticated'. Anon with the public anon key can then call /rest/v1/rpc/<fn>, or read and write the table if RLS is off or a policy is loose. With one careless migration, the answer keys or the bank are exposed to anyone.

findings.object: public.questions policy 'anon read live questions' (SELECT to anon, authenticated using status='live')
findings.what: The policy does nothing today, because anon and authenticated have no table or column SELECT grant on questions. All app reads go through supabaseAdmin() (data/question_reads.js, data/practice_source.js, data/nta_pool.js, src/lib/server/mob/deps.js, trapAtlas.js, revise.js, learning.js, the interact and upload routes). The policy is still a loaded gun: it is row-scoped only, so one 'grant select on questions to anon' (or the default-privilege issue above on a recreated table) would expose correct_answer, correct_index, explanation, evidence (signed records), author_id, uploaded_by and scoring fields for every live question to the public anon key.
findings.scenario: Someone runs 'grant select on public.questions to anon, authenticated' to fix a client-side read. Anyone can then call GET /rest/v1/questions?select=id,correct_answer,explanation&status=eq.live and download all answer keys before or during a mock, which defeats every timed mock and the leaderboard.
findings.migration:
drop policy if exists "anon read live questions" on public.questions;
-- RLS stays on with no policies: deny-all for anon and authenticated; service_role bypasses RLS.
findings.undo: create policy "anon read live questions" on public.questions for select to anon, authenticated using (status = 'live');

findings.object: question_interactions (insert path POST /api/questions/[id]/interact, src/app/api/questions/[id]/interact/route.js lines 148-179, queueReportedQuestion lines 183-198) -> public.questions.status
findings.what: Any signed-in student can take any live question out of the bank with a single 'report' interaction. The route accepts interaction_type 'report' from any user, runs no threshold, no dedupe, no rate limit (src/proxy.js excludes /api/ and there is no per-route limiter), and does not check that the student ever saw the question. queueReportedQuestion then sets questions.status='pending', verification_state='disputed', exploration_state='pending_review' for any status other than 'rejected'. The table itself is locked correctly (RLS on, 0 policies, only service_role grants). The weakness is the service-role route deciding on one report. Production today: 101 report rows from 40 users, up to 14 reports by one user in one day, 367 questions sitting at disputed/pending, 0 duplicate (user, question) report pairs.
findings.scenario: An attacker makes one free account. They pull question ids for every subject from the anonymous /api/questions/feed or /api/questions/explore, then script POST /api/questions/<id>/interact {interaction_type:'report', flow_context:'review'} for each one. All 6,683 live discoverable questions flip to pending within minutes. Practice, mocks and the 'unlimited mocks' bank go empty for every student until moderators restore each question by hand.

findings.object: question_scores (read path GET /api/questions/explore, src/app/api/questions/explore/route.js lines 116-133 and 96)
findings.what: The explore route needs no sign-in. It reads question_scores with the service-role client, embeds `questions!inner (*)` and returns those rows unchanged as `questions: merged`. readablePracticeQuestions (data/practice_library.js) only filters rows and strips nothing. The header comment 'FIX 10: strip correct_answer, explanation, recommended_difficulty from the explore response' is false: nothing is stripped. Anonymous callers get every questions column. That includes uploaded_by and author_id (user ids of contributors), provenance, evidence, legacy_screening, content_hash, family_id, exposure_budget/exposure_used, quality and AI scores, plus question_scores ranking internals (report_rate, skip_rate and others). /api/questions/feed already shows correct_answer and explanation by design, but feed maps rows to a curated shape. Explore returns the raw row. Status filtering is fine: the 1,068 rejected and 331 pending rows marked is_eligible_for_discovery are dropped in code.
findings.scenario: An unauthenticated client loops GET /api/questions/explore?subject=<each of 41 subjects>&limit=50 with the cursors. It collects contributor user ids (author_id/uploaded_by) tied to each question, internal provenance and evidence records, and the answer keys and explanations for the whole discoverable bank (about 6.7k live rows). With those user ids it can target or de-anonymise contributors, and it can read the internal moderation and quality signals.
findings.migration:
-- No SQL needed; code fix in src/app/api/questions/explore/route.js:
-- replace `questions!inner (*)` with an explicit list, e.g.
--   questions!inner (id, subject, chapter, difficulty, question, body, options, passage_text, passage_group_id, passage_id, order_index, tags, score, upvotes, downvotes, status, is_deleted, verification_state, exploration_state, legacy_screening, evidence, provenance, family_id, template_id?, correct_answer, explanation)
-- (keep only the fields readablePracticeQuestions needs), then before Response.json map each row to the same public shape /api/questions/feed returns
-- and drop author_id, uploaded_by, provenance, evidence, legacy_screening, content_hash, exposure_*, ai_*, quality_*, and the question_scores *_rate columns.
-- Fix or delete the misleading FIX 10 comment.
findings.undo: git revert <commit> of the explore route change (no database state changes).

findings.object: pg_default_acl for schema public (roles postgres and supabase_admin); affects any table/function recreated in this group
findings.what: Default privileges in schema public still give anon and authenticated ALL (arwdDxtm) on new tables, rwU on sequences and EXECUTE on new functions, for objects created by postgres and by supabase_admin. The 20261016170000 least-privilege migration revoked grants on existing objects but never changed defaults. The four tables and sync_question_scores_metadata are correctly locked today. But a migration that drops and recreates one of them (for example a question_bookmarks rebuild), or adds a helper function, silently hands anon and authenticated full grants again. Only RLS would then stand between them and the data, and a recreated function would have no RLS protection at all.
findings.scenario: A future migration does `create table public.user_question_progress_v2 (...)` and forgets `enable row level security`. The default ACL gives anon full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and anyone with the public anon key can read or rewrite every student's progress through PostgREST. Or a new SECURITY DEFINER helper over these tables becomes callable by anon through /rest/v1/rpc.

findings.object: question_interactions.user_id (no foreign key to public.users)
findings.what: question_interactions is the only per-student table in this group without a user_id FK. user_question_progress and question_bookmarks both cascade from users(id). There are 651 orphan rows today, all from 1 user_id that exists in neither public.users nor auth.users, dated 2026-04-22 to 2026-04-25 (probably a removed test or early account). accountDeletion.js deletes this table explicitly, but any other path that removes a users row (admin deletion, cleanup scripts, a cascade from auth) leaves behavioural data (seen, attempted, report notes in metadata) behind for a deleted person.
findings.scenario: An admin deletes a student from the dashboard or with SQL rather than through the account-deletion flow. Their users row and the progress and bookmarks rows go, but their interaction history, including free-text report notes, stays in question_interactions indefinitely. That conflicts with the deletion promise.
findings.undo: alter table public.question_interactions drop constraint if exists question_interactions_user_id_fkey;

findings.object: question_interactions.metadata / session_id (interact route, client-supplied)
findings.what: The interact route copies the client's metadata object (free text such as report 'note') and session_id into the row with no size or shape limit. The largest metadata today is 350 bytes. The route also accepts 'seen'/'attempted' for any existing question id, including pending or rejected ones, with any selected_key. That only affects the caller's own user_question_progress counters, so it is a data-quality issue, not cross-user access.
findings.scenario: A signed-in user posts 'seen' interactions with multi-hundred-KB metadata objects in a loop. Each one becomes a permanent row (question_interactions has no retention), which inflates storage, backups and egress. With no API rate limit, the only bound is request throughput.
findings.undo:
alter table public.question_interactions drop constraint if exists question_interactions_metadata_size;
alter table public.question_interactions drop constraint if exists question_interactions_session_id_len;

findings.object: Group summary: question_scores, user_question_progress, question_interactions, question_bookmarks, sync_question_scores_metadata() (no defect, for the record)
findings.what: Verified on production (isrxrxzjocewrdureyhp) with read-only queries. All four tables have RLS enabled (not forced) and 0 policies. Table grants go to service_role only. anon, authenticated and PUBLIC have no table grants and no column grants, and no views sit on these tables. question_bookmarks has 5 rows. sync_question_scores_metadata() is SECURITY INVOKER with search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp', EXECUTE for postgres and service_role only. It fires only through trigger trg_questions_sync_scores_metadata on public.questions and just copies subject/chapter/difficulty into question_scores. Running as invoker, it gives no privilege gain. The other functions that touch these tables (count_distinct_mock_sessions, finalise_expired_recovery_session, finish_recovery_session, start_learning_episode) are INVOKER, search_path pinned, with no anon or authenticated EXECUTE. Every code path in wt-audit17 uses the service-role client: supabaseAdmin(), or the `supabase` proxy that forwards to it. That covers bookmarks, learning/summary, questions/feed, questions/explore, questions/[id]/interact, internal/moderation/process (x-internal-secret), revise, repairCheckStore, mistakeRepair, getStudentAIContext, createAIRivalBattle, accountDeletion, data/db.js, practice_progress and nta_pool. Each scopes user_id from the verified session or JWT, never from the request body. No route lets one student read or change another student's progress, interactions or bookmarks, and anon cannot reach any of these tables through PostgREST.
findings.scenario: None. A signed-in student using the anon key plus their JWT against /rest/v1/user_question_progress, question_interactions, question_bookmarks or question_scores gets permission denied, because there are no grants. Cross-student access through the API routes is blocked because user_id always comes from the session.
findings.migration: None needed.
findings.undo: None.

findings.object: public schema default privileges (affects every future credit table and function)
findings.what: Checked read-only on production isrxrxzjocewrdureyhp. pg_default_acl for the public schema still gives anon and authenticated full rights on new objects. For role postgres, tables get arwdDxtm, functions get EXECUTE (X) and sequences get rwU, and supabase_admin has the same defaults. The three credit tables and five credit functions are safe today only because later migrations explicitly revoked those rights (20261016170000_browser_roles_least_privilege and the per-function revokes). No migration in wt-audit17/supabase/migrations runs ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. The current state is correct: RLS is on, there are 0 policies, and only service_role has grants on credit_transactions, user_daily_login_credits, user_question_answer_credits and users. The five functions have proacl {postgres=X, service_role=X}, so anon, authenticated and PUBLIC cannot EXECUTE them.
findings.scenario: A future migration adds a credit helper, for example CREATE FUNCTION public.mm_grant_bonus(p_user_id text, p_amount int) SECURITY DEFINER, and forgets the REVOKE. The default ACL makes it callable by anon and authenticated straight away. Any visitor holding the public anon key can then call POST /rest/v1/rpc/mm_grant_bonus {p_user_id:'<any id>', p_amount:100000} to mint credits for any account or drain someone else's. The same thing happens if someone adds a new credit table with a careless policy, because the table arrives with full DML grants for the browser roles.

findings.object: public.mm_spend_credits_amount(text,int,text,text)
findings.what: This is a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by postgres with search_path=public. pg_temp is not listed after public, but every relation in the body is schema-qualified (public.users), so it cannot be hijacked today. Only service_role and postgres can EXECUTE it. It subtracts p_amount from users.credit_balance but writes no credit_transactions row, and it ignores p_reference, so a retry is not idempotent. Its only caller is src/services/credits/checkAndConsumeCredits.js, which uses supabaseAdmin(). Nothing in wt-audit17 imports checkAndConsumeCredits, so it is dead code. It is also the only DEFINER function in this group, and DEFINER is not needed because service_role already bypasses RLS and holds UPDATE on users.
findings.scenario: If server code calls checkAndConsumeCredits again, every charge lowers the balance with no ledger line. The /api/me/credits history and the account-deletion 'keep' ledger (src/lib/server/accountDeletion.js:103) would then disagree with credit_balance. A network retry with the same reference charges twice, unlike spend_credits, which is protected by idx_credit_transactions_reference_unique. Anyone who later loosens its grants would also be exposing a DEFINER function that edits any user's balance from a caller-supplied p_user_id.

findings.object: credit_transactions, user_daily_login_credits, user_question_answer_credits (and the five functions): no fix needed
findings.what: Verified secure. All three tables have RLS on (not forced; the owner is postgres) and 0 policies. They have no grants to anon, authenticated or PUBLIC, and service_role has full DML. The users table, which holds credit_balance, also has no anon or authenticated grants. credit_transactions has a unique index on reference, so concurrent spend_credits or grant_contribution_credits calls with the same reference fail on the insert and roll back the balance change. spend_credits only allows the actions generate, attempt and attempt_full, at fixed amounts of 10, 10 and 50. grant_contribution_credits only allows contribute, for 15 credits. Both are INVOKER with search_path public, pg_temp. grant_daily_login_credits and grant_attempt_answer_credits are stubs that return false and 0, and their marker tables are dormant: 3 and 11 rows, with the last writes in April 2026. Code paths: data/db.js spendCredits and grantContributionCredits call supabaseAdmin().rpc. src/lib/server/practiceSessions.js:100 passes the session userId and a practice_<server id> reference. src/app/api/me/credits/route.js and src/lib/server/credits.js loadHistory read credit_transactions with supabaseAdmin, filtered by the session user id, and the cursor is checked against a regex before it goes into .or(). accountDeletion.js deletes the marker tables and keeps the ledger behind a users tombstone, so the ON DELETE CASCADE never fires. findings.object: creators.code lookup (src/lib/referrals/offers.js resolveCreatorCode; data/db.js getCreatorByCode)
findings.what: Referral codes are matched with .ilike('code', code). CODE_PATTERN (/^[a-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/) allows '_', and in ILIKE '_' matches any single character. A code made only of underscores therefore matches any creator code of the same length. On production there are active creators with codes of length 2, 3, 5 and 9, and two of the 5-character and two of the 9-character creators carry a Razorpay offer_id.
findings.scenario: A student on create-subscription or create-monthly-subscription enters the referral code '_____' (five underscores). normalizeCode accepts it, the ILIKE matches the first active 5-character creator, and the student gets that creator's Razorpay discount offer. The payment is also credited to that creator (creator_id, then creator_earning), so the creator earns payout money they never brought in. Anyone who tries lengths 2 to 9 gets a discount without knowing any real code. The admin duplicate-code check in /api/admin/creators uses the same lookup and can wrongly report a clash.
findings.migration: This is a code fix (codes are already stored lowercased and trimmed by createCreator). In offers.js and db.js getCreatorByCode, replace .ilike('code', code) with .eq('code', code). Optionally add a database guard against odd codes being stored (the existing rows pass it): ALTER TABLE public.creators ADD CONSTRAINT creators_code_format CHECK (code = lower(btrim(code)) AND code ~ '^[a-z0-9.-]{1,64}$') NOT VALID; ALTER TABLE public.creators VALIDATE CONSTRAINT creators_code_format; (If the owner wants '_' kept in codes, keep it in the regex. The .eq change alone closes the hole.) Also check: data/db.js getCreatorByEmail uses .ilike('email', ...) too. It is reachable only once the caller already has role 'creator', so it is low risk, but switch it to .eq on lower(email) as well.
findings.undo: Code: revert the commit. Database: ALTER TABLE public.creators DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS creators_code_format;

findings.object: public.create_pending_payout(text,text) [SECURITY INVOKER, search_path pinned to public, pg_temp; EXECUTE for postgres and service_role only]
findings.what: The function sums unpaid earnings, inserts a payouts row with status 'paid', then stamps payout_id on the matching payments. Nothing serializes two calls for the same creator. Under READ COMMITTED, a second call reads the same unpaid sum and inserts a second 'paid' payout for the same amount. Its UPDATE then waits for the first call and touches 0 rows. Permissions are otherwise right: anon and authenticated cannot execute it, it is not SECURITY DEFINER, and its search_path is pinned. Its only caller is POST /api/admin/payouts, behind requireAdmin, through supabaseAdmin.
findings.scenario: An admin double-clicks 'Mark paid', or two admins act at the same moment. Two payouts rows are recorded, each with status 'paid' and the full amount, but only one is linked to payments. The ledger then shows the creator paid twice, which can lead to a real double transfer or to wrong paidPayoutPaise totals. production payouts holds 0 rows today, so it has not happened yet.
findings.migration: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.create_pending_payout(p_creator_id text, p_actor_id text) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp' AS $function$ DECLARE v_payout_id TEXT; v_amount INTEGER; v_count INTEGER; BEGIN PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('create_pending_payout:' || p_creator_id)); SELECT COALESCE(SUM(creator_earning),0)::INTEGER, COUNT(*)::INTEGER INTO v_amount, v_count FROM public.payments WHERE creator_id = p_creator_id AND payout_id IS NULL AND payment_id IS NOT NULL AND amount_paid > 0 AND status IN ('captured','completed','paid') AND COALESCE(creator_earning,0) > 0; IF v_amount <= 0 OR v_count = 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'No unpaid earnings for creator %', p_creator_id USING ERRCODE = 'no_data_found'; END IF; INSERT INTO public.payouts (creator_id, amount, payment_count, status, paid_at, marked_paid_by) VALUES (p_creator_id, v_amount, v_count, 'paid', NOW(), p_actor_id) RETURNING id INTO v_payout_id; UPDATE public.payments SET payout_id = v_payout_id WHERE creator_id = p_creator_id AND payout_id IS NULL AND payment_id IS NOT NULL AND amount_paid > 0 AND status IN ('captured','completed','paid') AND COALESCE(creator_earning,0) > 0; RETURN v_payout_id; END; $function$; REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.create_pending_payout(text,text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_pending_payout(text,text) TO service_role;
findings.undo: Re-run the same CREATE OR REPLACE without the PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(...) line (that is the current production body, also in supabase/migrations/20260503220558_robust_referral_attribution.sql plus 20261016170300_function_search_path.sql). Grants stay as they are.

findings.object: Default privileges in schema public (pg_default_acl for postgres and supabase_admin) and the mm_ai_* functions and ai_credit_* tables that depend on them
findings.what: Live state is correct now. RLS is on for ai_credit_wallets, ai_credit_ledger and ai_credit_reservations, none of them has a policy, and anon and authenticated have no grants on them (only service_role does), so the tables are locked twice. All 7 mm_ai_* functions are SECURITY DEFINER, owned by postgres, pinned with search_path=public, refer to tables with the schema name, and only postgres and service_role can EXECUTE them. No view, trigger, publication or other function touches these tables. Every code path in wt-audit17 uses supabaseAdmin() with the user id taken from the session: replyDeps.js (reserve, mark_executing, commit, release), aiCreditWallet.js (consume, grant from the signature-checked Razorpay webhook with key ai_topup:order:payment), releaseExpired.js (cron /api/internal/finalise-sessions), and the reservation and ledger reads in credits.js, repairSaved.js, repairRecord.js, ruleBook.js, aiReplyReport.js, appPrefs.js, repairCheckStore.js and mistakeRepair.js. No user client touches this group. The risk is for the future. pg_default_acl gives anon and authenticated EXECUTE on every new function in public and ALL on every new table. The functions are safe today only because of explicit REVOKEs (20261002130000 lines 282-287, 0038 line 150, 20261016170200). CREATE OR REPLACE keeps the current ACL, but a DROP plus CREATE does not (for example, to change a signature).
findings.scenario: A future migration changes the signature of mm_ai_grant_bonus_credits (DROP FUNCTION, then CREATE) and forgets the REVOKE. The new function picks up the default grant, EXECUTE to anon and authenticated. Anyone holding the public anon key calls POST /rest/v1/rpc/mm_ai_grant_bonus_credits {p_user_id:'<own id>', p_amount:100000, ...} and gets unlimited paid AI credits. In the same way, an exposed mm_ai_reserve_credits or mm_ai_release_credits would let anyone drain or refund any student's wallet by user id. mm_ai_consume_credits already drifted this way once and needed 20261016170200.

findings.object: public.mm_ai_release_credits(text, text) (also reached through mm_ai_release_expired)
findings.what: When the wallet's period_start differs from the reservation's period_start (the month rolled over between reserve and release), the function adds the whole reservation amount, including the part taken from the free monthly allowance (from_included), to bonus_credits. Bonus credits never expire and are the paid pool. So a release that crosses midnight at month end turns free credits that would have expired into permanent paid-tier credits. The amount is bounded by the reservation size and needs a failed or expired operation, so the impact is small, but it is a credit-integrity leak and it breaks ledger reconciliation (wallet-reconciliation.mjs).
findings.scenario: Near 11:59 pm IST on the last day of the month, a student sends several PrepOS or repair requests with different requestIds. Each one reserves from the included allowance. Any of them that fails or is left to expire (for example, a provider error, or a function killed so that the cron sweep releases it after midnight) is released after the rollover. Its included credits come back as bonus_credits that carry over indefinitely, while the new month's included allowance has already been reset to full.

findings.object: All 7 mm_ai_* SECURITY DEFINER functions (search_path setting)
findings.what: Hardening only, not exploitable today. Each function sets search_path=public without pg_temp. When pg_temp is not listed, Postgres searches it first for relation names. Every table reference in these bodies has the public. prefix and built-in functions come from pg_catalog, and only service_role, which already has full access to the tables, can execute them. So no escalation exists today. An unqualified table name added in a future edit could be shadowed by a temporary table that the caller creates.
findings.scenario: A future edit adds an unqualified 'from ai_credit_wallets' to a definer function. A service_role session (or any role that is later granted EXECUTE) creates a temp table named ai_credit_wallets first, and the definer function reads attacker-controlled rows as postgres. Today nothing can trigger this.

findings.object: runtime_ai_requests (account deletion path, src/lib/server/accountDeletion.js:105-109)
findings.what: Account deletion 'anonymises' runtime_ai_requests by setting only user_id = null, but the student link and content stay in two other columns. (1) request_key for PrepOS calls is built as 'prepos:<userId>:<requestId>' (src/services/prepos/modelReply.js:18-21, src/lib/server/aiReplyReport.js:43-46), so the raw user UUID is still in the primary key. (2) receipt jsonb stores the full AI reply ({ response: result, usage }, src/services/ai/providerCore.js:259 and 284), and that reply is written from the student's context and message. Live production: 15 of 32 rows have receipt ? 'response', and 1 prepos row exists. RLS, grants and the guard functions are otherwise correct: RLS is on with 0 policies; anon and authenticated have no table, column or function grants; there are no views or realtime publications; all three functions are SECURITY INVOKER with search_path='' and EXECUTE for service_role only; every code path uses supabaseAdmin() on the server. This is a retention and erasure gap, not something an outside caller can reach.
findings.scenario: A student deletes their account. accountDeletion nulls user_id on their runtime_ai_requests rows. Afterwards, anyone with service-role or database access (an operator, a support export, a later breach of a backup) can still filter on request_key like 'prepos:<their uuid>:%' and read the AI replies written about them in receipt->'response'. That contradicts the deletion manifest's own claim ('the link to the student is removed, the cost rows stay') and a DPDP-style erasure promise.
findings.migration:
-- Fix part 1, the code: in src/lib/server/accountDeletion.js, call this RPC for runtime_ai_requests in place of the plain user_id=null update.
create or replace function public.anonymise_runtime_ai_requests(p_user_id text)
returns integer language sql security invoker set search_path='' as $$
  with u as (
    update public.runtime_ai_requests
       set user_id = null,
           request_key = 'deleted:' || md5(request_key),
           receipt = case when receipt is null then null else jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
                       'usage', receipt->'usage', 'error', receipt->'error', 'errorKind', receipt->'errorKind')) end
     where p_user_id is not null
       and (user_id = p_user_id or request_key like 'prepos:' || p_user_id || ':%')
    returning 1)
  select count(*)::int from u
$$;
revoke all on function public.anonymise_runtime_ai_requests(text) from public, anon, authenticated;
grant execute on function public.anonymise_runtime_ai_requests(text) to service_role;
-- Cost columns (reserved_usd, actual_usd, provider, model, created_at) are kept, so the monthly budget sums are unchanged.
-- Optional one-off backfill for accounts that were already deleted (review the count first with a select):
-- update public.runtime_ai_requests r set request_key='deleted:'||md5(r.request_key), receipt=jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object('usage',r.receipt->'usage','error',r.receipt->'error'))
--  where r.request_key like 'prepos:%' and not exists (select 1 from auth.users a where a.id::text = split_part(r.request_key,':',2));
findings.undo: drop function if exists public.anonymise_runtime_ai_requests(text); -- then revert the accountDeletion.js change. Rows already scrubbed cannot be restored (the hash and the removed reply are irreversible by design).

findings.object: public.mentor_messages via POST /api/ai/mentor/local (src/app/api/ai/mentor/local/route.js) plus findReceivedReply in src/lib/server/aiReplyReport.js and the study replay in src/app/api/ai/mentor/chat/route.js
findings.what: The /local route uses the service role to save a client-supplied `response` object as an 'assistant' message: structured_payload is the raw body.response, and content is body.response.reply. Nothing is whitelisted, so a student can write an assistant row carrying any charge.reference they like. Two server paths treat that field as proof that the model really replied. findReceivedReply (the Report-this-AI-reply route) matches structured_payload->charge->>reference = 'prepos:<userId>:<requestId>' and then lets the stored text override what the phone sent, because 'the stored text wins'. The chat route's duplicate-replay path for study lessons matches the same key and replays the stored payload. The data stays inside the student's own account, because user_id comes from the server session, so no student can reach another student's rows. What breaks is integrity: the Google Play AI-report record can be forged. Live DB check: 0 rows today with a non-model origin carrying a prepos reference, so there is no sign of use yet; 175 sessions came from local_assistant.

Reviewers and Play-policy evidence then quote AI output that was never generated. The same trick feeds a forged lesson payload into the study duplicate-replay path (self only).
findings.migration: No SQL can fix this, because the database cannot tell a service-role write from /local apart from one from /chat. Fix it in code. (1) In local/route.js, build the payload server-side instead of trusting the body: const safe = { reply: String(response.reply).slice(0, 4000), origin: 'local', cards: Array.isArray(response.cards) ? response.cards.slice(0, 6) : [], actions: Array.isArray(response.actions) ? response.actions.slice(0, 6).map(a => ({ label: String(a?.label || '').slice(0, 80), type: 'navigate', route: typeof a?.route === 'string' && a.route.startsWith('/') ? a.route.slice(0, 200) : '/today' })) : [] }; then save structured_payload: safe, so the client can never set charge, usage, study or origin. (2) In findReceivedReply and in the chat-route replay query, add .eq('structured_payload->>origin', 'model'). For the report route, also prefer the committed ai_credit_reservations row as the receipt. (3) Optional cleanup query to run before the fix ships (read-only check): select id from public.mentor_messages m join public.mentor_sessions s on s.id = m.session_id where s.metadata->>'source' = 'local_assistant' and m.structured_payload ? 'charge';

findings.object: public.mentor_messages (session ownership not enforced in the database)
findings.what: mentor_messages.user_id is free text, and the only foreign key is session_id -> mentor_sessions(id). findings.object: POST /api/questions/upload (src/app/api/questions/upload/route.js lines 125-139 and 172-176), which inserts moderation_jobs rows; checked against public.questions.content_hash and idx_questions_content_hash_unique
findings.what: A signed-in student can find the answer to any live question. The route hashes body + correct_answer with computeContentHash, looks the hash up using the service-role client, and replies 409 'An identical question already exists.' with duplicate_of set to the existing question's id. The unique index returns the same 409 through code 23505. I checked production with a select-only query: 861 of the 863 live questions that have a content_hash match this exact formula, and all 863 answers are one-character option keys. That means at most 4 to 6 guesses reveal the key. The route also has no rate limit. Every wrong guess inserts a pending question with the student as author, plus a moderation_jobs row. That is a cheap way to flood the queue (moderation_jobs already has about 8333 rows). The paid legacy worker is paused (process/route.js returns 503), so this does not spend money today. Leaving that aside, the group itself is locked down. All four tables have RLS on and no policies, and only service_role has grants: anon, authenticated and PUBLIC get no table, column or sequence grants. No views, triggers or realtime publication expose the tables. All four functions are SECURITY INVOKER with search_path pinned, and only postgres and service_role can EXECUTE them. Every code path uses the service-role client (supabaseAdmin or the supabase proxy, which forwards to the admin client). The internal moderation routes check x-internal-secret, /api/questions/moderate requires the moderator or admin role, and /api/ai/mentor/report requires a sign-in, applies a rate limit and checks ownership.
findings.scenario: A student starts a timed mock or arena paper and reads a question's body on screen. From the same signed-in session they POST /api/questions/upload with: that body, any valid subject/chapter pair, options [{key:'A'},{key:'B'},{key:'C'},{key:'D'}], and correct_answer 'A'. If the reply is 201, they try 'B', then 'C'. The guess that returns 409 with duplicate_of equal to the question id is the correct answer, so they answer correctly and climb the leaderboard. A script can do this for every question in a paper. Each wrong guess leaves a junk pending question and a queued moderation job behind.
findings.migration: No database change is needed; this is a code fix in src/app/api/questions/upload/route.js. (1) Stop telling the uploader whether a duplicate exists. When the hash already exists (from the pre-check or from error 23505), return the same 202 { status: 'pending_moderation' } a new upload gets, without duplicate_of and without inserting anything. Moderation already handles duplicates server-side. (2) Remove detail: questionError.message from the 500 response. (3) Add checkPersistentRateLimit per user to the route, the same way /api/ai/mentor/report does (for example 10 per minute and 50 per day). Optional extra protection: compute the dedupe hash from the body only, so the answer is never part of the probe.
findings.undo: Revert the route file to f725a422 with git checkout f725a422 -- src/app/api/questions/upload/route.js. Nothing in the database changes, so there is nothing to undo there.

findings.object: public.moderate_question_with_credit(text,text): SECURITY INVOKER, search_path public, pg_temp, EXECUTE for service_role only. Called from data/db.js moderateQuestion, which /api/questions/moderate calls for moderators and admins.
findings.what: The function approves any question with status 'pending'. It sets the question to live and verified and grants contribution credits to the author. It never checks evidence or open disputes itself. record_question_dispute puts disputed questions back to status 'pending' with verification_state 'disputed', so they are exactly the rows this function will approve. Today only the JavaScript publicationEligibility check in db.js stops this. The open dispute row is still the only thing hiding the question from students, and any reader that does not check disputes will serve a possibly wrong answer key.

findings.what: INFO, no exploitable problem found; this records the verified posture. Live production (isrxrxzjocewrdureyhp): all 4 tables have RLS on (not FORCE; owner is postgres) and 0 policies. Table grants: service_role has ALL; anon, authenticated and PUBLIC have none. No views, triggers or realtime publication entries reference these tables, so nothing exposes them through PostgREST, GraphQL or Realtime. All 5 functions are SECURITY INVOKER with search_path='' pinned and proacl {postgres=X, service_role=X}; has_function_privilege is false for anon and authenticated. The live function bodies match supabase/migrations/20261005185759_question_factory.sql byte for byte, apart from CRLF line endings. Dynamic SQL in publish_factory_question quotes every column name with format('%I') and passes values as a bound parameter ($1 via jsonb_populate_record), so it is not open to injection. The new questions.provenance and questions.legacy_screening columns, plus evidence and correct_answer, have no column SELECT or UPDATE grant for anon or authenticated. The 'anon read live questions' policy therefore cannot leak factory receipts. These tables hold no per-student rows, so no student can read or change another student's rows. Code paths in wt-audit17 all use the service role: src/lib/server/questionFactory.js (supabaseAdmin(); 'server-only'), reached only through src/app/api/admin/question-factory/route.js (requireAdmin on GET and POST; POST also requires same origin and caps the body at 1 MB) and src/app/admin/question-factory/page.jsx (requireAdmin). src/app/preview/question-factory/page.jsx calls notFound() in production and uses a local preview loader. The pipeline scripts (scripts/pipeline/factory.mjs, lib/factoryQueue.mjs, tools/*) use SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. requireAdmin trusts users.role. authenticated has no INSERT or UPDATE on users.role, so a student cannot promote themselves into the admin route that holds the service role.
findings.scenario: None. A signed-in student or anon caller using the anon key gets permission denied: on select from question_factory_jobs, on rpc('publish_factory_question'), and on rpc('claim_question_factory'). Even if EXECUTE were granted by mistake, the functions are INVOKER, so the caller would still lack the table privileges they need.

findings.object: public schema default privileges (affects any re-created question_factory_* table or factory function)
findings.what: pg_default_acl for both postgres and supabase_admin in schema public grants ALL on new tables (arwdDxtm) and EXECUTE on new functions to anon and authenticated. The factory objects are safe only because the migration runs an explicit revoke right after each create. If a later migration drops and re-creates any of these tables or functions (for example CREATE OR REPLACE after a DROP when a signature changes) and leaves out the revoke block, anon and authenticated get grants again automatically. RLS with 0 policies would still block table rows. A re-created function, though, would be EXECUTE-able by anon. Because these functions are INVOKER, that call would still fail on table privileges unless someone also switches one to SECURITY DEFINER. In that case anon could call publish_factory_question and insert live questions, or claim_question_factory and take the worker lease.
findings.scenario: A future migration runs `drop function publish_factory_question(jsonb,text,text); create function publish_factory_question(jsonb,text,text,text) ... security definer ...` with no revoke. Anon can then POST /rest/v1/rpc/publish_factory_question with a forged p_row and publish questions as status='live', bypassing app-side evidence signature checks. The function's DB guard only checks that evidence.signature is non-null.
findings.undo: alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public grant execute on functions to anon, authenticated, public;

findings.object: publish_factory_question(p_row jsonb, p_fingerprint text, p_job text)
findings.what: This is an integrity issue only, not a privilege issue: the caller is service_role only. The passage-group guard reads current_setting('mockmob.factory_group'), a custom setting that any session can set with set_config(), so a direct call can bypass the 'complete passage group required' check. The evidence gate also only checks that evidence.signature is non-null and that the policy_version and state strings match. It does not verify the signature cryptographically in the database. Any holder of the service-role key, such as a pipeline script bug or a leaked worker env, can therefore publish a passage child on its own, or a row with an unverified signature, as status='live'.
findings.scenario: A script holding the service-role key runs `select set_config('mockmob.factory_group','G1',true)` and then calls publish_factory_question with a row where passage_group_id='G1' and evidence.signature='x'. One orphan passage child goes live without its siblings or a valid signature. This requires the service-role key, so it is not reachable by students or anon.

findings.group: 16. Leaderboard, stats, analytics, rate limits and misc ops
findings.object: public schema default privileges (pg_default_acl for postgres and supabase_admin); affects any new table, function or sequence in this group
findings.what: I checked every table and function in group 16 on production (isrxrxzjocewrdureyhp, code f725a422) and found them locked down correctly. All 5 tables have RLS on and 0 policies. Only service_role holds table grants; anon and authenticated have none. All 9 functions are SECURITY INVOKER with search_path pinned (take_rate_limit uses ''). EXECUTE is granted only to postgres and service_role. Every code path calls them through supabaseAdmin() from server routes that check the session or admin role first: /api/events, /api/me/consent, /api/app/errors, the admin app-errors page, /api/leaderboard, rateLimit.js, funnelStore/funnelOnce, admin/audit.js and data/db.js. So a signed-in student cannot read or change another student's rows, and anon cannot reach anything here. The weak point is the default privileges behind that. For both postgres and supabase_admin they still grant ALL on new tables (arwdDxtm), EXECUTE on new functions and rwU on new sequences to anon and authenticated. These grants were removed from this group's objects one at a time. The sequences audit_logs_id_seq, usage_events_id_seq and app_errors_id_seq still carry rwU for anon and authenticated.
findings.scenario: A future migration adds, for example, usage_events_daily or a new SECURITY DEFINER helper such as app_errors_admin_view(), and forgets the explicit REVOKE. The new table gets anon SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (only RLS stands in the way, and a policy written as USING (true) for a service path would expose it). A new function is callable by anon through /rest/v1/rpc straight away. A SECURITY DEFINER analytics or audit reader would then leak audit_logs (actor emails, IPs) or usage_events to anyone holding the public anon key. The sequence grants also let anon or authenticated advance or reset the id sequences if they ever get a SQL path. That is low on its own, but it shows the defaults are open.

findings.group: 16. Leaderboard, stats, analytics, rate limits and misc ops
findings.object: persistent_rate_limits + take_rate_limit(text,int,int); src/lib/server/rateLimit.js checkPersistentRateLimit; src/lib/server/emailLoginPolicy.js
findings.what: persistent_rate_limits has 0 rows on production, even with 1,541 users and live email-code sign-in traffic. checkPersistentRateLimit only calls take_rate_limit when PERSISTENT_LIMITS_ENABLED === 'true'. Otherwise it falls back to a per-instance in-memory Map. So production appears to be running without the shared limits. These include the three email-code limits (20/hour per IP, 5/hour per IP+email, 15/hour per email) and the AI-report limits. docs/brain/STATUS.md:2046 lists this as still open. The database side is correct (service_role only, search_path ''), but it is never reached. A second, smaller gap: nothing purges expired buckets, there is no pg_cron on this project, and the bucket key is a hash of route + IP + key parts, so once enabled the table grows without bound.
findings.scenario: An attacker spreads requests to the email-code endpoint across Vercel serverless instances (each cold or parallel instance has its own empty Map). That sends far more than 15 codes an hour to one victim's inbox, which is email bombing and burns the sender's reputation and quota. It also allows more guesses or requests than the policy intends. The paid-model routes that rely on the persistent limit get the same per-instance multiplication.

findings.group: 16. Leaderboard, stats, analytics, rate limits and misc ops
findings.object: usage_events + purge_usage_events(int)
findings.what: purge_usage_events(retention_days default 180) exists and only service_role can run it. But nothing calls it in production code. The only reference is scripts/dev/check-staging-app-schema.mjs, and pg_cron is not installed, so the stated 180-day retention is not enforced. The function also does not clamp retention_days: a value of 0 or less deletes every row. The impact is limited because only service_role can call it. The table is empty today, account deletion removes a user's rows (accountDeletion.js:91 and FK ON DELETE CASCADE), and a consent withdrawal deletes them too, so this is a retention and compliance gap rather than an access hole.
findings.scenario: Once adults opt in, events pile up past 180 days, which contradicts the policy the consent screen points to. Separately, an operator or later script calls purge_usage_events(0) or a negative number by mistake and wipes all analytics.

findings.group: 16. Leaderboard, stats, analytics, rate limits and misc ops
findings.object: app_errors + app_error_record(jsonb); /api/app/errors
findings.what: Access is correct: the route requires a session and adult analytics consent, and only service_role can run app_error_record or app_errors_top. app_errors_top is read only by the admin page behind requireAdmin. Row size and day caps are in place: 2,000 new hashes a day, message up to 500 chars, stack up to 4 KB, count capped per row, and rows older than 30 days are deleted on the first insert of each day. The weak point is the limiter: /api/app/errors uses only the in-memory checkRateLimit. A consenting adult account can fill the day's 2,000-hash quota from many instances. Rows are not tied to a user, so once the daily cap is hit, real crash reports with new hashes are dropped for the rest of the day.
findings.scenario: One signed-in adult with consent scripts 2,000 random message_hash values early in the IST day, spread across serverless instances. Every real new crash that day is silently dropped (v_today >= 2000 means continue), so the owner loses crash visibility during a release.
findings.migration:
-- Code-side fix (no SQL needed): switch /api/app/errors to checkPersistentRateLimit with identityOnly + keyParts [userId] once PERSISTENT_LIMITS_ENABLED=true.
-- Optional DB guard: lower the per-call cap so one call cannot claim more than 50 new hashes.
-- (Re-create app_error_record with: if jsonb_array_length(p_rows) > 50 then p_rows := (select jsonb_agg(v) from (select v from jsonb_array_elements(p_rows) v limit 50) s); end if;)
